cat >> test/internals/reply.test.js <<'E'

test('reply.removeHeader removes headers set on the raw response', async t => {
  t.plan(7)
  const fastify = Fastify()
  fastify.get('/', (req, reply) => {
    reply.raw.setHeader('X-Powered-By', 'legacy')
    reply.header('x-other', 'a')
    t.assert.strictEqual(reply.hasHeader('x-powered-by'), true)
    reply.removeHeader('X-Powered-By')
    reply.removeHeader('X-Other')
    t.assert.strictEqual(reply.hasHeader('x-powered-by'), false)
    t.assert.strictEqual(reply.getHeader('x-powered-by'), undefined)
    t.assert.strictEqual('x-powered-by' in reply.getHeaders(), false)
    reply.send('ok')
  })

  const res = await fastify.inject('/')
  t.assert.strictEqual(res.statusCode, 200)
  t.assert.strictEqual(res.headers['x-powered-by'], undefined)
  t.assert.strictEqual(res.headers['x-other'], undefined)
})
E

content.text:
`reply.removeHeader()` now also removes headers set directly on `reply.raw`. I added a test for it, and the reply and related tests pass (298 passed, 0 failed). ESLint was clean on the two changed files.

- **Fix:** in `lib/reply.js`, `removeHeader` lowercases the name, deletes it from the reply's own headers, and calls `this.raw.removeHeader(key)` when `raw.headersSent === false`.
- **Why the guard:** Node throws if you remove a header after it has been flushed, so I skip the raw removal once headers have been sent.
- **Test:** the new test in `test/internals/reply.test.js` sets `X-Powered-By` on `reply.raw` and removes it with different casing. It checks `hasHeader`, `getHeader`, `getHeaders`, and the actual injected response.

I ran a subset of the suite: `test/internals/reply.test.js`, `test/reply-*.test.js`, `test/send.test.js`, `test/hooks.test.js` and `test/internals/handle-request.test.js`. I did not run the type tests or the whole `npm run unit` suite.
